title: Softmax and its Jacobian
summary: Compute softmax stably, then the matrix of derivatives that flows through it in backprop.
intro: **Softmax** turns scores z into probabilities: sᵢ = e^{zᵢ} / Σⱼ e^{zⱼ}. Subtracting max(z) first leaves the answer unchanged but stops e^{1000} overflowing to infinity.
Each output depends on every input, so the derivative is a matrix, the **Jacobian** J with Jᵢⱼ = ∂sᵢ/∂zⱼ. Working it out gives sᵢ(1 − sᵢ) on the diagonal and −sᵢsⱼ elsewhere: J = diag(s) − s sᵀ.
Every row of J adds up to 0 because the probabilities always add up to 1. Attention layers apply softmax to every row of scores, so this Jacobian sits in the backward pass of every transformer.
formula: sᵢ = e^{zᵢ − max z} / Σⱼ e^{zⱼ − max z}     J = diag(s) − s sᵀ
prompt: Write `softmax_jacobian(z)` that returns the Jacobian matrix of softmax at z as a nested list. Compute softmax stably.
hints: `np.outer(s, s)` is the matrix s sᵀ.
Check that every row adds up to zero.
explanation: With equal scores both probabilities are 0.5, so the diagonal is 0.5 × 0.5 = 0.25 and the off-diagonal is −0.25. For [1000, 1001] the naive version computes e^{1000}, which overflows; shifting by the max gives the same result as for [0, 1]. A single class has nothing to trade off with, so its Jacobian is 0.
